sections.title: Abstract
sections.originalMarkdown: Given the skewed nature of practical key-value (KV) storage workloads, distributed KV stores can adopt a tiered approach to support fast data access in a hot tier and persistent storage in a cold tier. To provide data availability guarantees for the hot tier, existing distributed KV stores often rely on replication and incur prohibitively high redundancy overhead. Erasure coding provides a low-cost redundancy alternative, but incurs high access performance overhead. We present ELECT, a distributed KV store that enables erasure coding tiering based on the log-structured merge tree (LSM-tree), by adopting a hybrid redundancy approach that carefully combines replication and erasure coding with respect to the LSM-tree layout. ELECT incorporates hotness awareness and selectively converts data from replication to erasure coding in the hot tier and offloads data from the hot tier to the cold tier. It also provides a tunable approach to balance the trade-off between storage savings and access performance through a single user-configurable parameter. We implemented ELECT atop Cassandra, which is replication-based. Experiments on Alibaba Cloud show that ELECT achieves significant storage savings in the hot tier, while maintaining high performance and data availability guarantees, compared with Cassandra.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.originalMarkdown:
Storage tiering provides a storage paradigm for balancing the trade-off between access performance and storage persistence in large-scale storage. In particular, for distributed key-value (KV) storage, practical KV workloads are known to have skewed access patterns [6, 9, 16, 62], in which a small fraction of KV pairs are frequently accessed (i.e., hot) and the remaining large fraction of KV pairs are rarely accessed (i.e., cold). Thus, it is natural for distributed KV stores to adopt storage tiering, in which a hot tier provides fast data access for hot KV pairs, while a cold tier provides persistent storage with less-demanding performance requirements for cold KV pairs.

A primary use case for storage tiering is edge-cloud storage. Our motivation is that Internet-of-things (IoT) applications are forecast to generate over 79.4 ZB of data in the wild by 2025 [51]. Since the cloud access performance is bottlenecked by the constrained Internet bandwidth, IoT applications are often coupled with the edge computing paradigm, in which edge nodes, the lightweight instances (e.g., micro-datacenters) provisioned with limited computation and storage resources, are deployed in close proximity to IoT devices [52, 53]. From a storage perspective, we can deploy a distributed KV store as the high-performance hot tier in the edge, while the cloud forms the persistent cold tier. Such an edge-cloud storage architecture has been used in virtualized network functions [40], multi-tier computing [42], multimedia management [21], etc. In addition to edge-cloud storage, storage tiering is also applicable to other storage architectures, such as content-delivery networks and cloud block storage (e.g., the combination of Amazon’s Elastic Block Store (EBS) [1] and Simple Storage Service (S3) [2]).

Providing data availability guarantees for hot-tier storage is necessary, especially when the hot tier is deployed in distributed storage environments where failures are prevalent [24]. For example, in edge-cloud storage, edge nodes have limited storage resources and are also prone to failures [53]. While the cloud provides abundant persistent storage resources, reconstructing any lost data for failed edge nodes from the cloud is inefficient due to the high edge-cloud latencies [12, 67]. Thus, to ensure data availability against edge node failures, the edge can introduce storage redundancy, so that any lost data in the edge can be directly reconstructed through the redundant data from other available edge nodes, without the need for retrieving data from the cloud for reconstruction. However, modern distributed KV stores [18, 22, 34, 46] are commonly designed for cloud data centers with sufficient resources, and adopt replication to distribute exact redundant copies for individual KV pairs across multiple nodes to provide fault tolerance against node failures. Replication multiplies storage overhead, which is prohibitive for resource-constrained edge nodes, or generally, the high-performance hot tier with limited storage resources.

Erasure coding provides a low-cost redundancy alternative to achieve data availability with much lower storage overhead compared with replication (see §2.3 for details). It has been extensively studied in the literature, especially for distributed KV storage in data centers (§7). However, there exists a fundamental storage-performance trade-off for replication and erasure coding: replication incurs high storage overhead, yet it supports not only load balancing of reads across redundant copies, but also simple reconstruction of any lost data from another available redundant copy; in contrast, erasure coding significantly reduces storage overhead, but it does not keep redundant copies for load balancing and is known to incur higher bandwidth and I/Os in reconstructing lost data when failures happen [19, 26]. It is thus critical to mitigate the storage overhead, while maintaining high access performance as if replication were used, in the hot tier.

We present ELECT, a distributed KV store that enables erasure coding tiering. ELECT builds on the log-structured merge tree (LSM-tree) [45]. Given the skewed nature of practical KV storage workloads [6, 9, 16, 62], ELECT extends the LSM-tree with a hybrid redundancy approach by storing limited amounts of hot KV pairs with replication in the hot tier for high access performance, while still achieving significant storage savings by storing large amounts of cold KV pairs with erasure coding in the hot tier. In addition, it can offload cold KV pairs from the hot tier to the cold tier to further alleviate the storage overhead in the hot tier.

Enabling hybrid redundancy in ELECT, however, is non-trivial. ELECT should decide how (e.g., at what granularities), when (e.g., on or off the write path), and what (e.g., differentiating hot and cold KV pairs) to convert replicated KV pairs into erasure-coded KV pairs. Most importantly, ELECT should provide a mechanism to balance the trade-off between storage savings and access performance; such a mechanism should be adaptive to various user requirements. Note that erasure coding has also been proposed for caching [49] and content delivery networks [61] in the context of storage tiering. The novelty of ELECT lies in the careful combination of replication and erasure coding for LSM-tree-based storage with several new design techniques (see §7 for details).

Our contributions are summarized as follows.

- We design ELECT to make a case for enabling erasure coding tiering for distributed KV storage. ELECT has several design features: (i) a redundancy transitioning approach for the conversion from replication to erasure coding based on the LSM-tree; (ii) a hotness-aware approach for both redundancy transitioning and the data offloading from the hot tier to the cold tier; and (iii) a tunable approach, with only a single user-specified parameter based on a storage saving target for simple deployment, for configuring how much data to be erasure-coded and offloaded.
- We implemented ELECT atop Cassandra v4.1.0 [3]. Cassandra [34] is a distributed KV store that uses consistent hashing [31] for data partitioning (§2.1) and the LSM-tree for internal storage management (§2.2). We choose Cassandra due to its decentralized, high-performance, and fault-tolerant nature. Cassandra supports only replication, and ELECT extends Cassandra with erasure coding tiering.
- We conduct experiments in an edge-cloud setting on Alibaba Cloud [38]. Compared with (replication-based) Cassandra, ELECT achieves 56.1% edge storage savings, with similar performance in normal read/write operations.

We now open-source our ELECT prototype at https://github.com/adslabcuhk/elect.
sections.translationMarkdown:
存储分层为大规模存储提供了一种在访问性能与存储持久性之间进行权衡的存储范式。具体而言，对于分布式键值（KV）存储，实际 KV 工作负载具有众所周知的偏斜访问模式 [6, 9, 16, 62]：一小部分 KV 对被频繁访问（即热数据），其余大部分 KV 对则很少被访问（即冷数据）。因此，分布式 KV 存储自然适合采用存储分层：热层为热 KV 对提供快速数据访问，冷层则以较低的性能要求为冷 KV 对提供持久存储。

存储分层的一个主要用例是边缘-云存储。我们的动机在于，据预测，到 2025 年，物联网（IoT）应用将在现实环境中产生超过 79.4 ZB 的数据 [51]。由于云端访问性能受限于有限的互联网带宽，IoT 应用通常会与边缘计算范式结合。在该范式中，边缘节点是仅配备有限计算与存储资源的轻量级实例（例如微型数据中心），被部署在靠近 IoT 设备的位置 [52, 53]。从存储角度看，我们可以在边缘部署分布式 KV 存储作为高性能热层，而由云端构成持久冷层。这种边缘-云存储架构已被用于虚拟化网络功能 [40]、多层计算 [42]、多媒体管理 [21] 等场景。除了边缘-云存储，存储分层也适用于其他存储架构，例如内容分发网络和云块存储（如结合 Amazon Elastic Block Store（EBS）[1] 与 Simple Storage Service（S3）[2]）。

有必要为热层存储提供数据可用性保证，尤其是在将热层部署于故障频发的分布式存储环境时 [24]。例如，在边缘-云存储中，边缘节点的存储资源有限，并且也容易发生故障 [53]。尽管云端提供了丰富的持久存储资源，但由于边缘与云之间的延迟较高，从云端为发生故障的边缘节点重建任何丢失数据都是低效的 [12, 67]。因此，为了在边缘节点故障时确保数据可用性，可以在边缘引入存储冗余。这样，边缘中丢失的任何数据都可以直接利用其他可用边缘节点上的冗余数据来重建，而无需从云端取回数据进行重建。然而，现代分布式 KV 存储 [18, 22, 34, 46] 通常面向资源充足的云数据中心设计，并采用复制机制，将每个 KV 对的完全相同冗余副本分布在多个节点上，以提供针对节点故障的容错能力。复制会成倍增加存储开销，这对于资源受限的边缘节点，或者更一般地说，对于存储资源有限的高性能热层而言，是难以承受的。

与复制相比，纠删码是一种低成本的冗余替代方案，能够以低得多的存储开销实现数据可用性（详见 §2.3）。文献已对其进行了广泛研究，特别是在数据中心的分布式 KV 存储领域（§7）。然而，复制与纠删码之间存在根本性的存储-性能权衡：复制会产生较高的存储开销，但它不仅支持在冗余副本之间对读请求进行负载均衡，还能利用另一个可用的冗余副本简单地重建任何丢失数据；相比之下，纠删码显著降低了存储开销，却不保留用于负载均衡的冗余副本，而且众所周知，在故障发生时重建丢失数据会产生更高的带宽和 I/O 开销 [19, 26]。因此，关键在于降低热层的存储开销，同时维持如同使用复制时一样的高访问性能。

我们提出 ELECT，这是一种支持纠删码分层的分布式 KV 存储。ELECT 构建在日志结构合并树（LSM-tree）[45] 之上。鉴于实际 KV 存储工作负载具有偏斜特征 [6, 9, 16, 62]，ELECT 使用混合冗余方法扩展 LSM-tree：在热层中通过复制存储少量热 KV 对，以获得较高访问性能；同时，在热层中通过纠删码存储大量冷 KV 对，从而仍能显著节省存储空间。此外，它还可以将冷 KV 对从热层卸载到冷层，以进一步缓解热层的存储开销。

然而，在 ELECT 中启用混合冗余并非易事。ELECT 应当决定以何种方式（例如采用何种粒度）、在何时（例如位于写入路径上还是写入路径之外），以及将哪些数据（例如区分热 KV 对与冷 KV 对）从复制转换为纠删码。最重要的是，ELECT 应当提供一种机制来平衡存储节省与访问性能之间的权衡；该机制应能适应不同的用户需求。需要指出的是，在存储分层场景中，也已有工作提出将纠删码用于缓存 [49] 和内容分发网络 [61]。ELECT 的新颖之处在于，它针对基于 LSM-tree 的存储谨慎地结合复制与纠删码，并提出了若干新的设计技术（详见 §7）。

我们的贡献总结如下。

- 我们设计 ELECT，以论证为分布式 KV 存储启用纠删码分层的可行性。ELECT 具有以下设计特性：(i) 一种基于 LSM-tree、将复制转换为纠删码的冗余转换方法；(ii) 一种具备热度感知能力的方法，同时用于冗余转换以及将数据从热层卸载到冷层；(iii) 一种可调方法，仅需一个基于存储节省目标的用户指定参数即可简化部署，并据此配置需要采用纠删码和卸载的数据量。
- 我们在 Cassandra v4.1.0 [3] 之上实现了 ELECT。Cassandra [34] 是一种分布式 KV 存储，使用一致性哈希 [31] 进行数据分区（§2.1），并使用 LSM-tree 进行内部存储管理（§2.2）。我们选择 Cassandra，是因为它具有去中心化、高性能和容错等特性。Cassandra 仅支持复制，而 ELECT 对其进行了扩展，使其支持纠删码分层。
- 我们在阿里云 [38] 的边缘-云环境中进行了实验。与（基于复制的）Cassandra 相比，ELECT 节省了 56.1% 的边缘存储空间，同时在正常读写操作中具有相近的性能。

我们现已将 ELECT 原型开源，地址为 https://github.com/adslabcuhk/elect。

sections.title: 2.1 Distributed KV Stores
sections.originalMarkdown:
Modern distributed KV stores partition KV pairs across multiple nodes by either consistent-hashing-based [31] distribution [17, 18, 22, 34] or range-based distribution [5, 11, 46, 57]. Consistent hashing arranges nodes in a hash ring, in which each node is associated with a range of the hash ring and stores the KV pairs whose keys are hashed to the range. For load balancing, each node can be further associated with multiple virtual nodes that are associated with different ranges of the hash ring. In contrast, range-based distribution divides the entire key space into non-overlapping ranges, in which each node stores the KV pairs in one of the ranges. ELECT builds on Cassandra [34], which uses consistent hashing, yet its design is compatible with both distribution approaches.

Replication is commonly used in distributed KV stores for fault tolerance [5, 11, 18, 22, 34, 46, 57]. Given a replication factor $R$, replication distributes $R$ copies of each KV pair across a set of nodes, which collectively form a replication group. Suppose that there are $M$ nodes (denoted by $N_0, N_1, ···, N_{R-1}$) arranged in a clockwise direction of a hash ring. Each node $N_i$ is associated with a non-overlapping key range $K_i$, where $0 ≤ i ≤ R - 1$, that corresponds to the keys that precede $N_i$ in the hash ring. Suppose that a KV pair is mapped to $N_i$. The first copy of the KV pair (called the primary replica) is stored in $N_i$, and the $R - 1$ additional copies (called the secondary replicas) are stored in the following nodes along the clockwise direction of the hash ring (i.e., $N_{i+1  mod M}, N_{i+2  mod M}, ···, N_{i+R-1  mod M}$). Thus, each node $N_i$ now manages the primary replicas of its associated key range as well as the secondary replicas of the associated key ranges of the $R - 1$ preceding nodes in the anti-clockwise direction of the hash ring. Figure 1 shows an example of triple replication (i.e., $R = 3$) and $M = 6$ nodes. For example, $N_0$ stores the KV pairs for $K_0$, $K_5$, and $K_4$.
sections.translationMarkdown:
现代分布式 KV 存储通过基于一致性哈希 [31] 的分布方式 [17, 18, 22, 34] 或基于范围的分布方式 [5, 11, 46, 57]，将 KV pair 划分到多个节点上。一致性哈希将节点排列在一个哈希环上，每个节点与哈希环上的一个范围相关联，并存储 key 的哈希值落在该范围内的 KV pair。为了实现负载均衡，每个节点还可以进一步关联多个虚拟节点，而这些虚拟节点分别关联哈希环上的不同范围。相比之下，基于范围的分布将整个 key space 划分为互不重叠的范围，每个节点存储其中一个范围内的 KV pair。ELECT 构建于采用一致性哈希的 Cassandra [34] 之上，但其设计与这两种分布方式均兼容。

分布式 KV 存储通常使用副本机制来提供容错能力 [5, 11, 18, 22, 34, 46, 57]。给定副本因子 $R$，副本机制会将每个 KV pair 的 $R$ 个副本分布到一组节点上，这些节点共同构成一个副本组。假设有 $M$ 个节点（记为 $N_0, N_1, ···, N_{R-1}$）沿哈希环顺时针排列。每个节点 $N_i$ 都关联一个不重叠的 key range $K_i$，其中 $0 ≤ i ≤ R - 1$；该范围对应哈希环上位于 $N_i$ 之前的 key。假设某个 KV pair 被映射到 $N_i$。该 KV pair 的第一个副本（称为主副本）存储在 $N_i$ 中，其余 $R - 1$ 个副本（称为次副本）存储在哈希环顺时针方向上随后的节点中（即 $N_{i+1  mod M}, N_{i+2  mod M}, ···, N_{i+R-1  mod M}$）。因此，每个节点 $N_i$ 现在既管理与自身关联的 key range 的主副本，也管理沿哈希环逆时针方向位于其之前的 $R - 1$ 个节点所关联 key range 的次副本。图 1 展示了一个三副本（即 $R = 3$）且包含 $M = 6$ 个节点的示例。例如，$N_0$ 存储 $K_0$、$K_5$ 和 $K_4$ 中的 KV pair。

sections.title: 2.2 Log-Structured Merge Trees (LSM-Trees)
sections.originalMarkdown:
Each node in Cassandra [34] manages its internal storage based on an LSM-tree [45], as also used in state-of-the-art local [9] and other distributed [5, 11, 34, 46] KV stores. An LSM-tree is a data structure designed for efficient writes (i.e., Put requests), reads (i.e., Get requests), and scans (i.e., Scan requests). Figure 1 shows how an LSM-tree is deployed in a distributed KV store. An LSM-tree organizes KV pairs in immutable fixed-size files, called SSTables, across $ℓ + 1$ levels, denoted by $L_0, L_1, ···, L_ℓ$; $L_0$ is the lowest level and $L_ℓ$ is the highest level. Each SSTable stores multiple KV pairs in a sorted manner in units of data blocks of size several KiB each. To support fast reads, each SSTable maintains an index block to track the key ranges and offsets of all data blocks as well as a Bloom filter [7] to track its currently stored keys with a small false positive rate. We refer to the data blocks as the data component, and collectively refer to the index block, Bloom filter, and SSTable metadata as the metadata component, for an SSTable. Inside the LSM-tree, the number of SSTables in each level increases from the lower to higher levels, while the KV pairs of an SSTable do not overlap with those of other SSTables in the same level except $L_0$ (note that some advanced LSM-trees may have overlapping KV pairs across SSTables in the same level [48]).

Writes and reads of KV pairs are issued to an LSM-tree as follows. Each write appends a newly written KV pair to an on-disk write-ahead log (WAL) for crash consistency and then inserts it into a mutable in-memory structure called a MemTable. When the MemTable is full, it is turned into an Immutable MemTable, which is then flushed to the lowest level $L_0$ as an SSTable. Each level has a capacity limit, increasing from lower to higher levels. When a lower level reaches its capacity limit, it triggers compaction to merge the KV pairs in the lower level into its next higher level. Specifically, a compaction operation selects an SSTable in the lower level, reads all SSTables in the higher level that have overlapping key ranges with the selected SSTable, sorts all the latest KV pairs (while all stale KV pairs are discarded), and re-generates and stores the non-overlapping SSTables in the higher level. On the other hand, each read for a key searches the MemTable and then the SSTables from $L_0$ to $L_ℓ$. It returns the KV pair if the key is found, or null otherwise.

Cassandra [34] 中的每个节点都基于一棵 LSM-tree [45] 管理其内部存储；先进的本地 KV 存储 [9] 和其他分布式 KV 存储 [5, 11, 34, 46] 也采用这种结构。LSM-tree 是一种为高效写入（即 Put 请求）、读取（即 Get 请求）和扫描（即 Scan 请求）而设计的数据结构。图 1 展示了 LSM-tree 在分布式 KV 存储中的部署方式。一棵 LSM-tree 将 KV pair 组织在不可变的定长文件（称为 SSTable）中，并分布于 $ℓ + 1$ 层，记为 $L_0, L_1, ···, L_ℓ$；$L_0$ 是最低层，$L_ℓ$ 是最高层。每个 SSTable 以若干 KiB 大小的数据块为单位，有序存储多个 KV pair。为支持快速读取，每个 SSTable 都维护一个 index block，用于记录所有 data block 的 key range 和 offset；同时还维护一个 Bloom filter [7]，以较低的 false-positive rate 记录当前存储的 key。对于一个 SSTable，我们将 data block 称为 data component，并将 index block、Bloom filter 和 SSTable metadata 统称为 metadata component。在 LSM-tree 内部，每层的 SSTable 数量从低层到高层逐渐增加；除 $L_0$ 外，同一层中某个 SSTable 的 KV pair 不会与其他 SSTable 的 KV pair 重叠（需要注意，一些高级 LSM-tree 可能允许同一层的不同 SSTable 包含相互重叠的 KV pair [48]）。

KV pair 的写入和读取按如下方式提交给 LSM-tree。每次写入首先将新写入的 KV pair 追加到磁盘上的 write-ahead log（WAL）以保证崩溃一致性，然后将其插入一个称为 MemTable 的可变内存结构。当 MemTable 写满时，它会转换为 Immutable MemTable，随后以 SSTable 的形式 flush 到最低层 $L_0$。每一层都有容量上限，并且容量从低层到高层逐渐增大。当较低层达到容量上限时，会触发 compaction，将该层中的 KV pair 合并到相邻的更高层。具体而言，一次 compaction 操作会在较低层选择一个 SSTable，读取较高层中 key range 与所选 SSTable 重叠的所有 SSTable，对所有最新的 KV pair 进行排序（同时丢弃全部过期 KV pair），然后在较高层重新生成并存储互不重叠的 SSTable。另一方面，对某个 key 的每次读取会先搜索 MemTable，再依次搜索从 $L_0$ 到 $L_ℓ$ 的 SSTable。如果找到该 key，则返回相应的 KV pair；否则返回 null。

sections.title: 2.3 Erasure Coding
sections.originalMarkdown:
Erasure coding provides low-redundancy fault tolerance for distributed storage. In this work, we focus on Reed-Solomon (RS) codes [50], configured by two parameters $n$ and $k$ (where $k < n$), as our erasure code construction. We choose RS codes for three reasons: (i) they support general coding parameters $n$ and $k$ (provided $k < n$); (ii) they have the minimum storage redundancy for tolerating against any $n - k$ node failures (a.k.a. the Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) property); and (iii) they have been popularly deployed in production [24, 43].

An $(n, k)$ RS code encodes $k$ original (uncoded) fixed-size data chunks into $n - k$ (coded) parity chunks of the same size, and the collection of $n$ data and parity chunks forms a coding group; the $(n, k)$ RS code considered here is systematic, meaning that the coding group keeps the $k$ data chunks. It ensures that any $k$ out of the $n$ chunks of a coding group can reconstruct all $k$ original data chunks. Large-scale storage systems comprise multiple coding groups that are independently encoded/decoded, and the $n$ chunks of each coding group are distributed across $n$ nodes to tolerate any $n - k$ node failures with $n/k×$ storage overhead. Compared with replication, RS codes incur much lower storage overhead with higher fault tolerance; for example, Facebook [43] uses the $(14, 10)$ RS code for four-node fault tolerance with $1.4×$ storage overhead only, while traditional triple replication [25] only provides two-node fault tolerance and incurs $3×$ storage overhead.

Erasure coding is known to have reconstruction penalty. For example, for any lost chunk, an $(n, k)$ RS code needs to retrieve $k$ available chunks from other alive nodes in the same coding group so as to decode the lost chunk. Reconstruction is common in practice due to the prevalence of failures [24, 26, 43], and there are two major reconstruction operations: degraded reads (i.e., reads issued to lost chunks) and full-node recovery (i.e., all data stored in a node is lost).

There are code constructions that reduce the reconstruction bandwidth of RS codes (e.g., regenerating codes [19] and locally repairable codes [26]). However, they still retrieve more data for reconstruction than the amount of lost data, and the trade-off between storage savings and reconstruction bandwidth in erasure coding is fundamental [19].

纠删码以较低的冗余为分布式存储提供容错能力。在本工作中，我们采用由两个参数 $n$ 和 $k$（其中 $k < n$）配置的 Reed-Solomon（RS）码 [50] 作为纠删码构造。我们选择 RS 码有三个原因：(i) 它支持通用的编码参数 $n$ 和 $k$（只要 $k < n$）；(ii) 它能以最小的存储冗余容忍任意 $n - k$ 个节点故障（又称最大距离可分（Maximum Distance Separable，MDS）性质）；(iii) 它已被广泛部署于生产环境 [24, 43]。

一个 $(n, k)$ RS 码将 $k$ 个原始（未编码）定长 data chunk 编码为 $n - k$ 个大小相同的（已编码）parity chunk，这 $n$ 个 data chunk 和 parity chunk 共同构成一个 coding group；本文考虑的 $(n, k)$ RS 码是系统码，这意味着 coding group 会保留这 $k$ 个 data chunk。它保证一个 coding group 的 $n$ 个 chunk 中任意 $k$ 个都能重建全部 $k$ 个原始 data chunk。大规模存储系统由多个彼此独立编码和解码的 coding group 组成；每个 coding group 的 $n$ 个 chunk 分布在 $n$ 个节点上，从而以 $n/k×$ 的存储开销容忍任意 $n - k$ 个节点故障。与副本机制相比，RS 码以低得多的存储开销实现更高的容错能力；例如，Facebook [43] 使用 $(14, 10)$ RS 码，只需 $1.4×$ 的存储开销即可容忍四个节点故障，而传统三副本机制 [25] 只能容忍两个节点故障，并产生 $3×$ 的存储开销。

纠删码存在众所周知的重建惩罚。例如，对于任意丢失的 chunk，$(n, k)$ RS 码都需要从同一 coding group 的其他存活节点取回 $k$ 个可用 chunk，才能解码出丢失的 chunk。由于故障十分普遍 [24, 26, 43]，重建在实践中很常见；重建操作主要有两种：降级读取（即对丢失 chunk 发起的读取）和整节点恢复（即某个节点中存储的全部数据均已丢失）。

一些编码构造可以降低 RS 码的重建带宽（例如 regenerating code [19] 和 locally repairable code [26]）。然而，它们在重建时取回的数据量仍然大于丢失的数据量，而且纠删码在存储节省与重建带宽之间的权衡是根本性的 [19]。

sections.title: 3 Design Considerations
sections.originalMarkdown:
Before we present the design of ELECT, we pose five design questions that need to be addressed.

**Q1: At what granularity should KV pairs be encoded?** In the context of KV stores, there are two approaches to encode KV pairs at different granularities: (i) self-encoding [8, 32, 33, 44], which splits a KV pair into $k$ fixed-size data chunks for encoding, and (ii) cross-encoding [14, 37, 65, 66], which aggregates multiple KV pairs into individual data chunks and performs encoding on each group of $k$ different data chunks. Self-encoding improves the parallelism of data access, but incurs significant metadata overhead for indexing all chunks of individual KV pairs [65], especially when KV services are dominated by small KV pairs [9]. In contrast, cross-encoding mitigates such metadata overhead, but the degraded read to a KV pair during a node failure needs to retrieve $k$ surviving chunks of the same coding group for reconstruction, thereby leading to amplified I/Os and bandwidth.

ELECT opts for cross-encoding to reduce the metadata overhead; if we only encode cold KV pairs that are rarely accessed (see Q3 below), the degraded read overhead should be limited. Also, since LSM-trees organize KV pairs in units of SSTables, ELECT opts for cross-encoding across multiple SSTables (i.e., each SSTable is treated as a chunk) to align with the LSM-tree-based storage management.

**Q2: Should erasure coding be performed on or off the write path?** Erasure coding for KV pairs can be performed inline [8, 20, 44], in which KV pairs are encoded on the write path, or offline [23, 36, 58], in which KV pairs are first written and later encoded in the background. Offline encoding has the flexibility of first storing hot KV pairs with replication for high access performance (see Q3 below). Thus, ELECT opts for offline encoding, in which KV pairs are first written with replication, and later performs erasure coding (across SSTables) in the background.

**Q3: How should skewed access patterns be addressed?** Practical KV workloads have skewed access patterns [6, 9, 16, 62], in which few KV pairs are frequently accessed (hot) and the majority of KV pairs are rarely accessed (cold). ELECT opts to apply erasure coding to cold SSTables to mitigate the degraded read overhead in cross-encoding (see Q1), while storing hot SSTables with replication for high-performance accesses with limited additional storage overhead. The idea of applying replication for hot data and erasure coding for cold data has been studied in prior studies [23, 36, 58], yet they target different deployment environments and how to adapt this idea into LSM-tree-based KV stores remains unexplored.

We motivate our design by examining the storage and access patterns of SSTables in different LSM-tree levels by generating realistic KV workloads using the benchmarking tool YCSB [16], which has been extensively used for KV storage evaluation in the literature. Specifically, we load 100 M 1-KiB KV pairs with a key size of 24 bytes and a value size of 1000 bytes into Cassandra (v4.1.0) via YCSB in our testbed (see §6.1 for testbed details). Also, using the `nodetool` command in Cassandra, we flush the MemTable of each LSM-tree to disk and force the compaction on all SSTables to keep all nodes in a stable state. We find that the last level (i.e., the highest level) is $L_4$, while $L_0$ is empty as the SSTables originally in $L_0$ are merged to $L_1$ after the forced compaction. We then issue 10 M reads to the stored KV pairs, where the keys are accessed under the Zipf distribution with a Zipfian constant of 0.99 (default in YCSB). Note that we set the replication factor as one to mitigate the impact of replication, and disable the key cache and row cache in Cassandra to have all KV pairs read from on-disk SSTables.

*Figure 2: Storage and access patterns in Cassandra.*

Figure 2(a) shows the distributions of numbers of SSTables and accesses to SSTables in each level. The intermediate levels $L_2$ and $L_3$ have high read frequencies. However, $L_4$ stores the most SSTables (56.2% of all SSTables), but only accounts for 10.2% of accesses. This motivates us to perform erasure coding only for the SSTables in the last level (e.g., $L_4$ in this example) and replication for the SSTables in the lower levels, so that we still achieve significant storage savings and limit the degraded read overhead caused by erasure coding.

Figure 2(b) further shows the cumulative distribution of access frequencies versus the SSTables in $L_4$. Only 18.2% of SSTables in $L_4$ are accessed. This suggests that we can apply erasure coding in a more fine-grained manner by selecting only the SSTables that are rarely accessed for erasure coding (i.e., with negligible degraded read overhead).

**Q4: How should the access overhead in the cold tier be mitigated?** It is expected that the cold tier has worse access performance than the hot tier. For example, in edge-cloud storage, while the cloud provides much more abundant storage resources than the edge, it is also limited by the high edge-cloud latency over the Internet (e.g., 30 ms for client-to-cloud communication versus 5 ms for client-to-edge communication [12, 67]). ELECT should selectively offload data that is rarely accessed from the hot tier to the cold tier, so as to avoid frequently retrieving the data back from the cold tier.

**Q5: How should ELECT address the trade-off between storage savings and access performance?** Both redundancy transitioning from replication to erasure coding and the data offloading from the hot tier to the cold tier in essence trade access performance for storage savings. ELECT should provide a tunable mechanism that allows users to balance the trade-off depending on their requirements.
sections.translationMarkdown:
在介绍 ELECT 的设计之前，我们先提出五个需要解决的设计问题。

**Q1：应以何种粒度对 KV pair 进行编码？** 在 KV 存储的语境下，有两种以不同粒度编码 KV pair 的方法：(i) self-encoding [8, 32, 33, 44]，即将一个 KV pair 拆分为 $k$ 个定长 data chunk 后进行编码；(ii) cross-encoding [14, 37, 65, 66]，即将多个 KV pair 分别聚合到单独的 data chunk 中，再对每组 $k$ 个不同的 data chunk 进行编码。self-encoding 提高了数据访问的并行度，但为每个 KV pair 的所有 chunk 建立索引会产生显著的 metadata 开销 [65]，尤其是在 KV 服务以小型 KV pair 为主时 [9]。相比之下，cross-encoding 缓解了这类 metadata 开销；但节点发生故障时，对某个 KV pair 的降级读取需要取回同一 coding group 中 $k$ 个存活的 chunk 来进行重建，从而放大 I/O 和带宽开销。

ELECT 选择 cross-encoding 以降低 metadata 开销；如果只编码很少被访问的冷 KV pair（见下文 Q3），降级读取开销应当是有限的。此外，由于 LSM-tree 以 SSTable 为单位组织 KV pair，ELECT 选择跨多个 SSTable 执行 cross-encoding（即将每个 SSTable 视为一个 chunk），以便与基于 LSM-tree 的存储管理相适配。

**Q2：纠删码应在写路径上执行，还是在写路径之外执行？** KV pair 的纠删码可以 inline 执行 [8, 20, 44]，即在写路径上对 KV pair 进行编码；也可以 offline 执行 [23, 36, 58]，即先写入 KV pair，随后在后台对其进行编码。offline encoding 可以灵活地先通过副本机制存储热 KV pair，以提供较高的访问性能（见下文 Q3）。因此，ELECT 选择 offline encoding：KV pair 首先通过副本机制写入，随后在后台进行纠删码编码（跨 SSTable 编码）。

**Q3：应如何处理倾斜的访问模式？** 实际 KV workload 的访问模式具有倾斜性 [6, 9, 16, 62]，即少量 KV pair 被频繁访问（热），而大多数 KV pair 很少被访问（冷）。ELECT 选择对冷 SSTable 应用纠删码，以缓解 cross-encoding 的降级读取开销（见 Q1）；同时通过副本机制存储热 SSTable，以有限的额外存储开销实现高性能访问。此前的研究 [23, 36, 58] 已探讨过对热数据使用副本、对冷数据使用纠删码的思路，但这些工作针对的是不同的部署环境；如何将这一思路应用于基于 LSM-tree 的 KV 存储仍未得到探索。

为了说明设计动机，我们使用 benchmark 工具 YCSB [16] 生成真实的 KV workload，并考察不同 LSM-tree 层级中 SSTable 的存储和访问模式；YCSB 已在文献中被广泛用于 KV 存储评估。具体而言，我们在测试平台中通过 YCSB 将 1 亿个 1 KiB 的 KV pair 加载到 Cassandra（v4.1.0）中，其中 key 大小为 24 bytes，value 大小为 1000 bytes（测试平台详情见 §6.1）。此外，我们使用 Cassandra 的 `nodetool` 命令，将每棵 LSM-tree 的 MemTable flush 到磁盘，并对所有 SSTable 强制执行 compaction，使所有节点保持稳定状态。我们发现最后一层（即最高层）是 $L_4$；由于强制 compaction 后原本位于 $L_0$ 的 SSTable 被合并到 $L_1$，因此 $L_0$ 为空。随后，我们对所存储的 KV pair 发起 1000 万次读取；key 按 Zipf 分布访问，Zipfian constant 为 0.99（YCSB 的默认值）。需要注意的是，我们将副本因子设为 1 以减小副本机制的影响，并禁用 Cassandra 中的 key cache 和 row cache，使所有 KV pair 都从磁盘上的 SSTable 中读取。

*图 2：Cassandra 中的存储与访问模式。*

图 2(a) 展示了各层中 SSTable 数量以及对 SSTable 访问次数的分布。中间层 $L_2$ 和 $L_3$ 的读取频率较高。然而，$L_4$ 存储的 SSTable 最多（占全部 SSTable 的 56.2%），但仅占访问次数的 10.2%。这促使我们只对最后一层的 SSTable（本例中为 $L_4$）使用纠删码，而对较低层的 SSTable 使用副本机制，从而在实现显著存储节省的同时，限制纠删码导致的降级读取开销。

图 2(b) 进一步展示了访问频率相对于 $L_4$ 中 SSTable 的累积分布。$L_4$ 中仅有 18.2% 的 SSTable 被访问。这表明我们可以以更细的粒度应用纠删码，只选择很少被访问的 SSTable 进行纠删码编码（即降级读取开销可以忽略）。

**Q4：应如何缓解冷层中的访问开销？** 可以预期，冷层的访问性能比热层更差。例如，在边缘-云存储中，云端虽然能提供远比边缘端丰富的存储资源，但也受限于互联网上较高的边缘-云延迟（例如，client-to-cloud 通信延迟为 30 ms，而 client-to-edge 通信延迟为 5 ms [12, 67]）。ELECT 应当有选择地将很少被访问的数据从热层 offload 到冷层，从而避免频繁地从冷层取回数据。

**Q5：ELECT 应如何处理存储节省与访问性能之间的权衡？** 无论是从副本机制转换为纠删码的 redundancy transitioning，还是从热层向冷层进行 data offloading，本质上都是以访问性能换取存储节省。ELECT 应当提供一种可调机制，使用户能够根据自身需求平衡这一权衡。

sections.title: 4 ELECT Design
sections.originalMarkdown:
ELECT extends Cassandra [34], which uses replication for fault tolerance, with erasure coding tiering. It is deployed across multiple nodes in the hot tier and is backed by the cold tier with persistent storage. It proposes several design elements to address the questions in §3.

- **LSM-tree-based redundancy transitioning (§4.1).** ELECT applies cross-encoding (see Q1) across SSTables in an offline manner (see Q2), by converting SSTables from replication into erasure coding (called redundancy transitioning). It decouples the replicas originating from different nodes into multiple LSM-trees, such that it applies cross-encoding to the primary replicas and removes the secondary replicas after encoding. One subtlety is that it should maintain the correctness of redundancy transitioning even under LSM-tree compaction, which changes the content of SSTables.
- **Hotness awareness (§4.2).** ELECT applies cross-encoding to only SSTables in the last LSM-tree level (see Q3). It also offloads SSTables that tend to be rarely accessed from the hot tier to the cold tier to mitigate the access overhead in the cold tier (see Q4).
- **Balancing storage-performance trade-off (§4.3).** ELECT provides a user-configurable parameter, namely the storage saving target, to balance the trade-off between storage savings and access performance (see Q5).

ELECT 在 Cassandra [34] 的基础上引入纠删码分层；Cassandra 使用复制来实现容错。ELECT 部署在热层的多个节点上，并由具有持久存储的冷层提供后端支持。它提出了若干设计要素，以解决第 3 节中的问题。

- **基于 LSM-tree 的冗余转换（§4.1）。** ELECT 以离线方式（见 Q2）对多个 SSTable 应用交叉编码（见 Q1），将 SSTable 的冗余形式从复制转换为纠删码（称为冗余转换）。它将源自不同节点的副本解耦到多个 LSM-tree 中，从而对主副本应用交叉编码，并在编码后删除次副本。一个需要谨慎处理的问题是，即使 LSM-tree compaction 改变了 SSTable 的内容，也必须维持冗余转换的正确性。
- **热度感知（§4.2）。** ELECT 仅对 LSM-tree 最后一层中的 SSTable 应用交叉编码（见 Q3）。它还将往往很少被访问的 SSTable 从热层卸载到冷层，以减轻冷层中的访问开销（见 Q4）。
- **平衡存储—性能权衡（§4.3）。** ELECT 提供一个用户可配置参数，即存储节省目标，用于平衡存储节省与访问性能之间的权衡（见 Q5）。

sections.title: 4.1.1 LSM-tree Management
sections.originalMarkdown:
**Decoupled replication management.** In Cassandra, all replicas stored in a node are managed in a single LSM-tree. To facilitate cross-SSTable encoding across nodes and subsequent removals of replicas, ELECT borrows the idea of decoupled replication management [57, 68] (originally designed for reducing I/O amplification) by separating the replicas into multiple LSM-trees in each node. Recall that for a replication factor $R$, each node maintains the primary replicas originating from the node itself and the secondary replicas originating from the $R - 1$ preceding nodes in the hash ring (§2.1). ELECT now lets each node maintain $R$ LSM-trees, comprising one primary LSM-tree for the primary replicas and $R - 1$ secondary LSM-trees for the $R - 1$ respective sets of secondary replicas. For example, in Figure 1 with $R = 3$, $N_0$ writes the primary replicas in key range $K_0$ to the primary LSM-tree and the secondary replicas in key ranges $K_5$ and $K_4$ to two other secondary LSM-trees.

**LSM-tree level generation.** The original LSM-tree creates a new level $L_\ell$ when the current last level $L_{\ell-1}$ is full. However, depending on the current storage usage, the last level $L_\ell$ may only contain a small number of SSTables. This compromises the effectiveness of ELECT, which applies erasure coding only to the SSTables in the last level. To address this issue, ELECT modifies the current LSM-tree design and creates the new level $L_\ell$ in the LSM-tree only when the size of the current last level $L_{\ell-1}$ reaches the capacity limit of the next level $L_\ell$. For example, the LSM-tree in Cassandra currently sets the size limits of $L_{\ell-1}$ and $L_\ell$ as $T$ and $10T$, respectively, where $T$ is some capacity limit and the default capacity difference across adjacent levels is 10×. ELECT now keeps adding SSTables to $L_{\ell-1}$ even though the size exceeds $T$. It only creates $L_\ell$ when the size of $L_{\ell-1}$ exceeds $10T$. It then still keeps a size $T$ of SSTables in $L_{\ell-1}$ and moves at least $9T$ of SSTables to $L_\ell$. In this case, ELECT ensures that the last level $L_\ell$ always contains a sufficiently large number of SSTables (almost 90% of all SSTables across all levels in our case) and maintains the effectiveness of redundancy transitioning. Note that if the LSM-tree grows and adds a new level, the current erasure-coded SSTables in the previous last level will be moved to the new last level.

**解耦的副本管理。** 在 Cassandra 中，一个节点上存储的所有副本都由单个 LSM-tree 管理。为了便于跨节点进行跨 SSTable 编码以及随后删除副本，ELECT 借鉴了解耦副本管理 [57, 68] 的思想（最初是为降低 I/O 放大而设计），将每个节点中的副本分离到多个 LSM-tree 中。回顾一下，当复制因子为 $R$ 时，每个节点维护源自该节点自身的主副本，以及源自 hash ring 中前面 $R - 1$ 个节点的次副本（§2.1）。ELECT 让每个节点维护 $R$ 个 LSM-tree，其中一个 primary LSM-tree 用于主副本，另有 $R - 1$ 个 secondary LSM-tree，分别用于 $R - 1$ 组次副本。例如，在图 1 中，当 $R = 3$ 时，$N_0$ 将键范围 $K_0$ 中的主副本写入 primary LSM-tree，并将键范围 $K_5$ 和 $K_4$ 中的次副本分别写入另外两个 secondary LSM-tree。

**LSM-tree 层级生成。** 原始 LSM-tree 在当前最后一层 $L_{\ell-1}$ 已满时创建新层 $L_\ell$。然而，根据当前的存储使用情况，最后一层 $L_\ell$ 可能只包含少量 SSTable。这会削弱 ELECT 的有效性，因为 ELECT 只对最后一层中的 SSTable 应用纠删码。为解决这一问题，ELECT 修改了现有 LSM-tree 设计：只有当当前最后一层 $L_{\ell-1}$ 的大小达到下一层 $L_\ell$ 的容量上限时，才在 LSM-tree 中创建新层 $L_\ell$。例如，Cassandra 中的 LSM-tree 当前将 $L_{\ell-1}$ 和 $L_\ell$ 的大小上限分别设为 $T$ 和 $10T$，其中 $T$ 是某个容量上限，相邻层之间默认的容量差为 10×。现在，即使 $L_{\ell-1}$ 的大小超过 $T$，ELECT 仍继续向其中添加 SSTable。只有当 $L_{\ell-1}$ 的大小超过 $10T$ 时，它才创建 $L_\ell$。随后，它仍在 $L_{\ell-1}$ 中保留大小为 $T$ 的 SSTable，并将至少 $9T$ 的 SSTable 移动到 $L_\ell$。这样，ELECT 可确保最后一层 $L_\ell$ 始终包含足够多的 SSTable（在我们的案例中，接近所有层中全部 SSTable 的 90%），从而维持冗余转换的有效性。请注意，如果 LSM-tree 增长并增加一个新层，原先最后一层中当前采用纠删码的 SSTable 将被移动到新的最后一层。

sections.title: 4.1.2 Parity Node Selection
sections.originalMarkdown:
ELECT applies cross-SSTable encoding on $k$ uncoded SSTables (called data SSTables) from $k$ nodes (called data nodes) and generates $n - k$ coded SSTables (called parity SSTables) that are stored in $n - k$ nodes (called parity nodes). Before encoding, ELECT first selects the set of parity nodes to which the parity SSTables are distributed. The selection process should satisfy the following requirements: (i) for fault tolerance, the parity nodes should be distinct from the data nodes; (ii) for load balancing, the parity SSTables are evenly distributed across all nodes after parity node selection; and (iii) for scalability, the parity nodes can be deterministically selected by individual nodes without centralized coordination.

To satisfy the above requirements, ELECT forms each coding group over $n$ consecutive nodes in the hash ring, say $N_{i \bmod M}, N_{(i+1) \bmod M}, \cdots, N_{(i+n-1) \bmod M}$ for $0 \le i < M$, where $M$ is the total number of nodes, the first $k$ nodes are the data nodes, and the following $n - k$ nodes are the parity nodes. Also, each node locally maintains a monotonic sequence number $Q$ (initialized as zero). Specifically, for each SSTable in the primary LSM-tree that is selected by $N_i$ ($0 \le i < M$) for erasure coding, $N_i$ selects a leader parity node $N_p$, which will be responsible for computing and sending the parity SSTables (§4.1.3) to $n - k - 1$ other parity nodes. It computes $p$ as:

$$p = (i + (Q \bmod k) + 1) \bmod M, \tag{1}$$

and increments the sequence number $Q$ by one for each SSTable being selected for erasure coding. Note that the selection of SSTables is based on their priorities (§4.2).

We explain via an example the idea behind Equation (1). From Figure 1 (where $M = 6$), we use (6, 4) RS coding. Thus, $N_0$ (deterministically) selects a leader parity node from $N_1$, $N_2$, $N_3$, and $N_4$ in a round-robin fashion for encoding its SSTables as $Q$ increases; similarly, $N_1$ selects a leader parity node from $N_2$, $N_3$, $N_4$, and $N_5$, and so forth. Inversely, each node $N_i$ ($0 \le i < M$) in the whole system will be selected as a leader parity node by $k$ nodes $N_{(i-1) \bmod M}, N_{(i-2) \bmod M}, \cdots, N_{(i-k) \bmod M}$, which now become the $k$ data nodes of a coding group; for example, in Figure 3, $N_4$ serves as a leader parity node for $N_0$, $N_1$, $N_2$, and $N_3$ in a coding group under (6, 4) RS coding. Since a large-scale storage system typically contains multiple coding groups, ELECT ensures that all coding groups are distributed across different sequences of $n$ consecutive nodes. Finally, each leader parity node (say $N_p$) will be the first parity node of a coding group, and the remaining $n - k - 1$ parity nodes of the coding group are the $n - k - 1$ succeeding nodes of $N_p$ along the clockwise direction of the hash ring.

ELECT 对来自 $k$ 个节点（称为数据节点）的 $k$ 个未编码 SSTable（称为数据 SSTable）应用跨 SSTable 编码，生成 $n - k$ 个编码后的 SSTable（称为校验 SSTable），并将它们存储在 $n - k$ 个节点（称为校验节点）中。在编码之前，ELECT 首先选择用于分布校验 SSTable 的校验节点集合。选择过程应满足以下要求：(i) 为实现容错，校验节点应不同于数据节点；(ii) 为实现负载均衡，在选择校验节点后，校验 SSTable 应均匀分布在所有节点上；(iii) 为实现可扩展性，各个节点应能以确定性方式选择校验节点，而无需集中式协调。

为满足上述要求，ELECT 在 hash ring 中的 $n$ 个连续节点上构成每个编码组。对于 $0 \le i < M$，这些节点记为 $N_{i \bmod M}, N_{(i+1) \bmod M}, \cdots, N_{(i+n-1) \bmod M}$，其中 $M$ 是节点总数，前 $k$ 个节点为数据节点，接下来的 $n - k$ 个节点为校验节点。此外，每个节点都在本地维护一个单调递增的序列号 $Q$（初始化为零）。具体而言，对于 primary LSM-tree 中由 $N_i$（$0 \le i < M$）选中进行纠删码编码的每个 SSTable，$N_i$ 都会选择一个 leader 校验节点 $N_p$；该节点负责计算校验 SSTable，并将其发送给另外 $n - k - 1$ 个校验节点（§4.1.3）。$p$ 的计算方式为：

$$p = (i + (Q \bmod k) + 1) \bmod M, \tag{1}$$

每选中一个 SSTable 进行纠删码编码，就将序列号 $Q$ 加一。请注意，SSTable 的选择以其优先级为依据（§4.2）。

我们通过一个例子解释公式 (1) 背后的思想。在图 1（其中 $M = 6$）中，我们使用 (6, 4) RS 编码。因此，随着 $Q$ 增大，$N_0$ 以轮询方式从 $N_1$、$N_2$、$N_3$ 和 $N_4$ 中（确定性地）选择一个 leader 校验节点，以对其 SSTable 进行编码；类似地，$N_1$ 从 $N_2$、$N_3$、$N_4$ 和 $N_5$ 中选择一个 leader 校验节点，依此类推。反过来，整个系统中的每个节点 $N_i$（$0 \le i < M$）都会被 $k$ 个节点 $N_{(i-1) \bmod M}, N_{(i-2) \bmod M}, \cdots, N_{(i-k) \bmod M}$ 选为 leader 校验节点，而这 $k$ 个节点便成为一个编码组的 $k$ 个数据节点；例如，在图 3 中，在 (6, 4) RS 编码下，$N_4$ 作为由 $N_0$、$N_1$、$N_2$ 和 $N_3$ 构成的一个编码组的 leader 校验节点。由于大规模存储系统通常包含多个编码组，ELECT 确保所有编码组分布在由不同连续 $n$ 个节点构成的序列上。最后，每个 leader 校验节点（例如 $N_p$）将成为一个编码组的第一个校验节点，而该编码组中其余 $n - k - 1$ 个校验节点，则是 hash ring 顺时针方向上紧随 $N_p$ 的 $n - k - 1$ 个节点。

sections.title: 4.1.3 Cross-SSTable Encoding
sections.originalMarkdown:
**Encoding workflow.** Each of the $k$ data nodes of a coding group sends an SSTable to the leader parity node, which is determined by the sequence number $Q$ according to Equation (1) (§4.1.2). Upon receiving the $k$ data SSTables, the leader parity node encodes them into $n - k$ parity SSTables, stores one of the parity SSTables locally, and sends the remaining parity SSTables to the other $n - k - 1$ parity nodes. The parity nodes store the parity SSTables as separate files outside of their LSM-trees. For example, from Figure 3, consider a coding group for (6, 4) RS coding with $k = 4$ data nodes $N_0$, $N_1$, $N_2$, and $N_3$, all of which share the same leader parity node $N_4$. $N_0$ sends an SSTable (say $S$) to $N_4$. Then, $N_4$ encodes $S$ together with other SSTables (from $N_1$, $N_2$, and $N_3$, respectively) to generate the parity SSTables (say $P$ and $P'$). $N_4$ stores $P$ locally and sends $P'$ to another parity node $N_5$.

The leader parity node also generates a metadata structure, called ECMeta, for the coding group to support failure reconstruction (§5). The ECMeta contains $n$ 4-tuples, each of which describes a data/parity SSTable in the coding group, including: (i) the cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA-256) of the content of the data component of the SSTable (32 bytes), (ii) the SSTable size (4 bytes), (iii) the identifier of the node that stores the SSTable (4 bytes), and (iv) the position in the coding group (indexed from 0 to $n - 1$) (4 bytes). In particular, we borrow the idea from deduplication [47] and use the SSTable hash as the unique identifier to search for the SSTable during reconstruction, assuming that the hash collisions for distinct SSTables are practically unlikely. The leader parity node then sends the ECMeta of each data SSTable to the corresponding $R$ nodes in the replication group. Upon receiving the ECMeta, each of the $R$ nodes includes the ECMeta in the metadata component of the corresponding SSTable.

**Compaction-triggered parity updates.** When a primary LSM-tree undergoes compaction, its data SSTables (in the last level) may be updated. ELECT needs to update the parity SSTables of the same coding group to maintain consistency.

Consider a primary LSM-tree that undergoes compaction. Let $S_0, S_1, \cdots, S_u$ be the old data SSTables before compaction, and $S'_0, S'_1, \cdots, S'_v$ be the new data SSTables after compaction, where $u$ and $v$ are the numbers of old data SSTables and new data SSTables, respectively. Without loss of generality, the two sequences of data SSTables $(S_0, S_1, \cdots, S_u)$ and $(S'_0, S'_1, \cdots, S'_v)$ are ordered by (non-overlapping) key ranges. ELECT pairs each of the old and new data SSTables as $(S_0, S'_0), (S_1, S'_1)$, and so forth. If $u < v$ (i.e., there exist more new data SSTables), the extra new data SSTables are simply added as regular SSTables to the primary LSM-tree without erasure coding; if $u > v$ (i.e., there exist fewer new data SSTables due to deleted KV pairs), ELECT pairs each extra old data SSTables with zero-filled dummy SSTables. The dummy SSTables can later be replaced by the new data SSTables that correspond to the same leader parity node.

For each pair of old and new SSTables, ELECT reads the ECMeta of the old data SSTable to identify the corresponding leader parity node. It sends the pair to the leader parity node, which updates the parity SSTables of the same coding group based on delta-based parity updates (similar to read-modify-writes in RAID) [10] and sends out the updated ECMeta.

**编码工作流程。** 一个编码组中的每个数据节点都向 leader 校验节点发送一个 SSTable；该 leader 校验节点由序列号 $Q$ 根据公式 (1)（§4.1.2）确定。收到 $k$ 个数据 SSTable 后，leader 校验节点将它们编码为 $n - k$ 个校验 SSTable，在本地存储其中一个校验 SSTable，并将其余校验 SSTable 发送给另外 $n - k - 1$ 个校验节点。校验节点将校验 SSTable 作为独立文件存储在其 LSM-tree 之外。例如，考虑图 3 中采用 (6, 4) RS 编码的一个编码组，它有 $k = 4$ 个数据节点 $N_0$、$N_1$、$N_2$ 和 $N_3$，这些节点共享同一个 leader 校验节点 $N_4$。$N_0$ 将一个 SSTable（记为 $S$）发送给 $N_4$。随后，$N_4$ 将 $S$ 与其他 SSTable（分别来自 $N_1$、$N_2$ 和 $N_3$）一起编码，生成校验 SSTable（记为 $P$ 和 $P'$）。$N_4$ 在本地存储 $P$，并将 $P'$ 发送给另一个校验节点 $N_5$。

leader 校验节点还会为该编码组生成一种名为 ECMeta 的元数据结构，用于支持故障重建（§5）。ECMeta 包含 $n$ 个四元组，每个四元组描述编码组中的一个数据/校验 SSTable，其中包括：(i) SSTable 数据组件内容的密码学 hash（例如 SHA-256，32 字节）；(ii) SSTable 大小（4 字节）；(iii) 存储该 SSTable 的节点标识符（4 字节）；以及 (iv) 该 SSTable 在编码组中的位置（索引范围从 0 到 $n - 1$，4 字节）。具体而言，我们借鉴去重 [47] 的思想，使用 SSTable hash 作为唯一标识符，以便在重建期间查找 SSTable，并假设不同 SSTable 在实践中几乎不会发生 hash 冲突。随后，leader 校验节点将每个数据 SSTable 的 ECMeta 发送给复制组中对应的 $R$ 个节点。收到 ECMeta 后，这 $R$ 个节点中的每个节点都将 ECMeta 纳入对应 SSTable 的元数据组件中。

**Compaction 触发的校验更新。** 当 primary LSM-tree 执行 compaction 时，它的数据 SSTable（位于最后一层）可能被更新。ELECT 需要更新同一编码组中的校验 SSTable，以维持一致性。

考虑一个执行 compaction 的 primary LSM-tree。令 $S_0, S_1, \cdots, S_u$ 为 compaction 前的旧数据 SSTable，令 $S'_0, S'_1, \cdots, S'_v$ 为 compaction 后的新数据 SSTable，其中 $u$ 和 $v$ 分别是旧数据 SSTable 和新数据 SSTable 的数量。不失一般性，两个数据 SSTable 序列 $(S_0, S_1, \cdots, S_u)$ 和 $(S'_0, S'_1, \cdots, S'_v)$ 都按（互不重叠的）键范围排序。ELECT 将每个旧数据 SSTable 与新数据 SSTable 配对为 $(S_0, S'_0), (S_1, S'_1)$，依此类推。如果 $u < v$（即新数据 SSTable 更多），则额外的新数据 SSTable 直接作为普通 SSTable 加入 primary LSM-tree，不采用纠删码；如果 $u > v$（即由于 KV pair 被删除，新数据 SSTable 更少），ELECT 会将每个额外的旧数据 SSTable 与一个填零的虚拟 SSTable 配对。之后，可以用对应于同一 leader 校验节点的新数据 SSTable 替换这些虚拟 SSTable。

对于每一对新旧 SSTable，ELECT 读取旧数据 SSTable 的 ECMeta，以识别对应的 leader 校验节点。它将这一对 SSTable 发送给 leader 校验节点；后者根据基于 delta 的校验更新（类似于 RAID 中的 read-modify-write）[10]，更新同一编码组的校验 SSTable，并发出更新后的 ECMeta。

sections.title: 4.1.4 Secondary Replica Removal
sections.originalMarkdown:
ELECT removes the secondary replicas from the secondary LSM-trees after cross-SSTable encoding to reclaim storage space. Since the LSM-trees of different nodes perform compaction asynchronously, they may have distinct SSTables. It is important to avoid incorrectly removing KV pairs from the secondary replicas, especially for the KV pairs that are updated after cross-SSTable encoding.

After cross-SSTable encoding, for each primary LSM-tree, ELECT generates a key list for each data SSTable, where the key list includes the keys in the SSTables and the corresponding written timestamps; note that the timestamps are already provided by Cassandra to identify the latest versions of KV pairs among replicas. It sends the key list to the other secondary LSM-trees that contain the secondary replicas of the data SSTable. For each secondary LSM-tree, ELECT finds all SSTables in the last level whose KV pairs are covered by the key list. It removes only the KV pairs that are either the current or older versions with respect to the timestamps specified in the key list. Note that ELECT creates new SSTables and tracks the key ranges of the removed KV pairs in the metadata components of the new SSTables, so as to be compatible with the LSM-tree management under replication. Finally, it reconstructs the SSTables for the remaining KV pairs. If the current versions of all KV pairs indicated by the key list are removed, the key list is also removed.

Figure 4(a) shows the replica removal workflow in the last level of a secondary LSM-tree. Suppose that the secondary LSM-tree has four KV pairs in the last level $L_\ell$, denoted by $KV_0$, $KV_1$, $KV_2$, and $KV_3$, whose keys are $k_0$, $k_1$, $k_2$, and $k_3$, respectively, while the four KV pairs are stored in two SSTables $(KV_0, KV_1)$ and $(KV_2, KV_3)$. Now, suppose that the secondary LSM-tree receives a key list $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$, whose timestamps indicate that $KV_1$ is the current version (i.e., same timestamp), $KV_2$ is older, and $KV_3$ is newer. Thus, ELECT removes $KV_1$ and $KV_2$. It also creates an SSTable that tracks the key ranges for the deleted $KV_1$ and $KV_2$.

Note that the secondary LSM-tree may not remove the current version of a KV pair (e.g., $KV_2$) as indicated in the key list, as the KV pair to be removed is not yet moved to the last level due to asynchronous compaction of different nodes. Figure 4(b) shows a case where the second last level $L_{\ell-1}$ has a newer version $KV_1$ and the current version $KV_2$ with respect to the timestamps in the key list. During compaction, ELECT removes $KV_2$ and adds $KV_1$ to the last level $L_\ell$.

*Figure 4: Secondary replica removal in ELECT.*

在跨 SSTable 编码后，ELECT 从 secondary LSM-tree 中删除次副本，以回收存储空间。由于不同节点的 LSM-tree 异步执行 compaction，它们可能具有不同的 SSTable。必须避免错误地从次副本中删除 KV pair，尤其是那些在跨 SSTable 编码后被更新的 KV pair。

跨 SSTable 编码后，对于每个 primary LSM-tree，ELECT 为每个数据 SSTable 生成一个 key list，其中包含 SSTable 中的键及其对应的写入时间戳；请注意，Cassandra 已提供这些时间戳，用于识别各个副本中 KV pair 的最新版本。ELECT 将 key list 发送给包含该数据 SSTable 次副本的其他 secondary LSM-tree。对于每个 secondary LSM-tree，ELECT 找出最后一层中所有 KV pair 被 key list 覆盖的 SSTable。它只删除相对于 key list 中所指定时间戳而言属于当前版本或更旧版本的 KV pair。请注意，ELECT 会创建新的 SSTable，并在新 SSTable 的元数据组件中记录被删除 KV pair 的键范围，以便与复制模式下的 LSM-tree 管理兼容。最后，它为剩余 KV pair 重建 SSTable。如果 key list 所指示的全部 KV pair 的当前版本均已删除，则该 key list 也会被删除。

图 4(a) 展示了 secondary LSM-tree 最后一层中的副本删除工作流程。假设 secondary LSM-tree 的最后一层 $L_\ell$ 中有四个 KV pair，分别记为 $KV_0$、$KV_1$、$KV_2$ 和 $KV_3$，其键分别为 $k_0$、$k_1$、$k_2$ 和 $k_3$；这四个 KV pair 存储在两个 SSTable $(KV_0, KV_1)$ 和 $(KV_2, KV_3)$ 中。现在，假设 secondary LSM-tree 收到 key list $(k_1, k_2, k_3)$，其时间戳表明 $KV_1$ 是当前版本（即时间戳相同）、$KV_2$ 更旧，而 $KV_3$ 更新。因此，ELECT 删除 $KV_1$ 和 $KV_2$。它还会创建一个 SSTable，用于记录已删除的 $KV_1$ 和 $KV_2$ 的键范围。

请注意，secondary LSM-tree 可能不会删除 key list 所指示的某个 KV pair 的当前版本（例如 $KV_2$），因为不同节点异步执行 compaction，待删除的 KV pair 尚未被移动到最后一层。图 4(b) 展示了这样一种情况：相对于 key list 中的时间戳，倒数第二层 $L_{\ell-1}$ 中存在较新的版本 $KV_1$ 和当前版本 $KV_2$。在 compaction 期间，ELECT 删除 $KV_2$，并将 $KV_1$ 加入最后一层 $L_\ell$。

*图 4：ELECT 中的次副本删除。*

sections.title: 4.2 Hotness Awareness
sections.originalMarkdown:
ELECT incorporates hotness awareness into redundancy transitioning and data offloading.

**Hotness-aware redundancy transitioning.** ELECT monitors the hotness of each SSTable based on two metrics: (i) the access frequency, which refers to the number of reads issued to the SSTable as measured by Cassandra, and (ii) the lifetime, which refers to the elapsed time since the SSTable creation. Among the SSTables in the last level of the primary LSM-tree in each node, an SSTable is said to have a higher priority to be selected for encoding (§4.1.3) if it has a lower access frequency and (if a tie exists) a longer lifetime. ELECT selects the SSTables with higher priorities for encoding based on a storage saving target (§4.3).

**Cold-data offloading.** ELECT dynamically offloads SSTables from the hot tier to the cold tier based on the hotness of SSTables, so as to further mitigate the storage overhead in the hot tier. First, it offloads parity SSTables with long lifetimes as they only affect parity updates (§4.1.3) and failure reconstruction. Second, after all parity SSTables are offloaded, it selectively offloads the data SSTables with higher priorities. The exact numbers of data and parity SSTables being offloaded depend on a storage saving target (§4.3). Note that if an SSTable is selected to be offloaded, only the SSTable’s data component is moved, while its metadata component remains in the hot tier to serve read and compaction operations. Furthermore, when a read or compaction operation touches an SSTable in the cold tier, ELECT retrieves the SSTable’s data component from the cold tier to the hot tier.

ELECT 将热度感知融入冗余转换和数据卸载。

**热度感知的冗余转换。** ELECT 基于两个指标监控每个 SSTable 的热度：(i) 访问频率，即由 Cassandra 测得的、向该 SSTable 发起的读取次数；(ii) 生命周期，即从该 SSTable 创建以来经过的时间。在每个节点的主 LSM-tree 最后一层中的 SSTable 里，如果某个 SSTable 的访问频率更低，并且在访问频率相同时生命周期更长，则认为它被选中进行编码（§4.1.3）的优先级更高。ELECT 根据存储节省目标（§4.3），选择优先级较高的 SSTable 进行编码。

**冷数据卸载。** ELECT 根据 SSTable 的热度，动态地将 SSTable 从热层卸载到冷层，从而进一步降低热层的存储开销。首先，它会卸载生命周期较长的奇偶校验 SSTable，因为这些 SSTable 只会影响奇偶校验更新（§4.1.3）和故障重建。其次，在所有奇偶校验 SSTable 都被卸载之后，它会有选择地卸载优先级较高的数据 SSTable。具体卸载多少个数据 SSTable 和奇偶校验 SSTable，取决于存储节省目标（§4.3）。需要注意的是，如果某个 SSTable 被选中卸载，只会移动该 SSTable 的数据组件，其元数据组件仍保留在热层，以服务读取和 compaction 操作。此外，当读取或 compaction 操作访问冷层中的 SSTable 时，ELECT 会将该 SSTable 的数据组件从冷层取回热层。

sections.title: 4.3 Balancing Storage-Performance Trade-Off
sections.titleTranslation: 4.3 平衡存储与性能之间的权衡
sections.originalMarkdown:
Redundancy transitioning and data offloading alleviate the storage overhead in the hot tier, yet they also incur performance overhead compared with replicating all data in the hot tier. To balance the trade-off between the storage savings and access performance, ELECT introduces a configurable storage saving target $\alpha$ with respect to when all SSTables are replicated, so as to control the number of SSTables involved in redundancy transitioning and data offloading. Specifically, $\alpha$ is a fractional value between zero and one, such that a larger $\alpha$ implies that more SSTables are erasure-coded and offloaded from the hot tier to the cold tier, and vice versa.

**Quantifying storage overhead.** We approximate the storage overhead in the hot tier based on the number of SSTables in a single primary LSM-tree in a node. Let $C_{all}$ be the total number of SSTables in the primary LSM-tree, $C_{last}$ be the number of SSTables in the last level of the LSM-tree, $C_{rt}$ be the number of data SSTables in the last level being converted from replication to erasure coding, and $C_{pm}$ and $C_{dm}$ be the numbers of parity SSTables and data SSTables being offloaded to the cold tier, respectively.

We now quantify the actual storage size of a replication group (in terms of the number of SSTables), assuming that the storage load is balanced (i.e., all nodes have the same number of SSTables in their respective primary LSM-trees). ELECT replicates $C_{all}-C_{rt}$ SSTables and encodes $C_{rt}$ SSTables, so their storage usage is $(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}$. It also offloads $C_{pm}+C_{dm}$ SSTables to the cold tier. Thus, the actual storage size of a replication group is:

$$
(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}-C_{pm}-C_{dm}. \tag{2}
$$

When all SSTables are replicated, the actual storage size of a replication group is $C_{all}\cdot R$. To achieve the storage saving target $\alpha$, our goal is to configure $C_{rt}$, $C_{pm}$, and $C_{dm}$, so that

$$
1-\frac{1}{C_{all}\cdot R}[(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}-C_{pm}-C_{dm}]\geq\alpha. \tag{3}
$$

In ELECT, each node computes $C_{rt}$, $C_{pm}$, and $C_{dm}$ independently (without centralized coordination) given $C_{all}$, $C_{last}$, and $\alpha$. Assuming balanced storage loads, the respective values of $C_{all}$ and $C_{last}$ across nodes have very small differences.

**Balancing trade-off.** ELECT starts with redundancy transitioning to keep all SSTables (replicated or erasure-coded) in the hot tier. If $\alpha$ is not met, it offloads parity SSTables to the cold tier, so that all SSTables remain accessible from the hot tier when no failure occurs; in case of a node failure, parity SSTables are needed for recovery. If $\alpha$ is still not met, ELECT offloads data SSTables to the cold tier. Note that ELECT only offloads erasure-coded SSTables to the cold tier, so $\alpha$ may not be achievable if it is too large.

- *Case 1 (Redundancy transitioning):* ELECT sets $C_{pm}=C_{dm}=0$ and chooses the largest possible $C_{rt}$ to maximize storage savings. Note that $C_{rt}\leq C_{last}$. From Equation (3), $C_{rt}$ is given by:

  $$
  C_{rt}=\min\left\{\frac{R\cdot C_{all}\cdot\alpha}{R-n/k},C_{last}\right\}. \tag{4}
  $$

- *Case 2 (Offloading of parity SSTables):* ELECT proceeds to Case 2 if $\alpha$ is not met, i.e., $C_{rt}=C_{last}$. It sets $C_{dm}=0$ and chooses the largest possible $C_{pm}$. Note that the number of parity SSTables is at most $\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}$. From Equation (3), $C_{pm}$ is given by:

  $$
  C_{pm}=\min\left\{R\cdot C_{all}\cdot\alpha-\left(R-\frac{n}{k}\right)\cdot C_{last},\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}\right\}. \tag{5}
  $$

- *Case 3 (Offloading of data SSTables):* ELECT proceeds to Case 3 if $\alpha$ is still not met, i.e., $C_{pm}=\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}$. It chooses the largest possible $C_{dm}$. Note that $C_{dm}\leq C_{last}$. From Equation (3), $C_{dm}$ is given by:

  $$
  C_{dm}=\min\left\{C_{all}\cdot R\cdot\alpha-(R-1)\cdot C_{last},C_{last}\right\}. \tag{6}
  $$
sections.translationMarkdown:
冗余转换和数据卸载减轻了热层的存储开销，但与将所有数据都以副本形式存储在热层相比，它们也会引入性能开销。为了平衡存储节省与访问性能之间的权衡，ELECT 以所有 SSTable 均采用副本存储时的情况为基准，引入了一个可配置的存储节省目标 $\alpha$，从而控制参与冗余转换和数据卸载的 SSTable 数量。具体而言，$\alpha$ 是一个介于 0 和 1 之间的小数值；$\alpha$ 越大，意味着越多 SSTable 会采用纠删码，并从热层卸载到冷层，反之亦然。

**量化存储开销。** 我们根据节点内单个主 LSM-tree 中 SSTable 的数量，近似计算热层的存储开销。令 $C_{all}$ 表示主 LSM-tree 中 SSTable 的总数，$C_{last}$ 表示 LSM-tree 最后一层中的 SSTable 数量，$C_{rt}$ 表示最后一层中从副本转换为纠删码的数据 SSTable 数量，$C_{pm}$ 和 $C_{dm}$ 分别表示卸载到冷层的奇偶校验 SSTable 数量和数据 SSTable 数量。

现在，我们量化一个复制组的实际存储大小（以 SSTable 数量表示），并假设存储负载均衡，即所有节点各自的主 LSM-tree 都具有相同数量的 SSTable。ELECT 对 $C_{all}-C_{rt}$ 个 SSTable 采用副本存储，并对 $C_{rt}$ 个 SSTable 进行编码，因此它们的存储用量为 $(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}$。它还将 $C_{pm}+C_{dm}$ 个 SSTable 卸载到冷层。因此，一个复制组的实际存储大小为：

$$
(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}-C_{pm}-C_{dm}. \tag{2}
$$

当所有 SSTable 都采用副本存储时，一个复制组的实际存储大小为 $C_{all}\cdot R$。为了达到存储节省目标 $\alpha$，我们的目标是配置 $C_{rt}$、$C_{pm}$ 和 $C_{dm}$，使得

$$
1-\frac{1}{C_{all}\cdot R}[(C_{all}-C_{rt})\cdot R+C_{rt}\cdot\frac{n}{k}-C_{pm}-C_{dm}]\geq\alpha. \tag{3}
$$

在 ELECT 中，给定 $C_{all}$、$C_{last}$ 和 $\alpha$，每个节点独立计算 $C_{rt}$、$C_{pm}$ 和 $C_{dm}$，且无需集中式协调。假设存储负载均衡，不同节点各自的 $C_{all}$ 和 $C_{last}$ 值只有很小的差异。

**平衡权衡。** ELECT 首先执行冗余转换，使所有 SSTable（采用副本或纠删码）都保留在热层。如果未达到 $\alpha$，它会将奇偶校验 SSTable 卸载到冷层，使得在未发生故障时，所有 SSTable 仍可从热层访问；当节点发生故障时，则需要奇偶校验 SSTable 进行恢复。如果仍未达到 $\alpha$，ELECT 会将数据 SSTable 卸载到冷层。需要注意的是，ELECT 只会将采用纠删码的 SSTable 卸载到冷层，因此，如果 $\alpha$ 过大，可能无法达到该目标。

- *情况 1（冗余转换）：* ELECT 设置 $C_{pm}=C_{dm}=0$，并选择尽可能大的 $C_{rt}$，以最大化存储节省。需要注意的是，$C_{rt}\leq C_{last}$。根据公式 (3)，$C_{rt}$ 为：

  $$
  C_{rt}=\min\left\{\frac{R\cdot C_{all}\cdot\alpha}{R-n/k},C_{last}\right\}. \tag{4}
  $$

- *情况 2（卸载奇偶校验 SSTable）：* 如果未达到 $\alpha$，即 $C_{rt}=C_{last}$，则 ELECT 进入情况 2。它设置 $C_{dm}=0$，并选择尽可能大的 $C_{pm}$。需要注意的是，奇偶校验 SSTable 的数量至多为 $\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}$。根据公式 (3)，$C_{pm}$ 为：

  $$
  C_{pm}=\min\left\{R\cdot C_{all}\cdot\alpha-\left(R-\frac{n}{k}\right)\cdot C_{last},\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}\right\}. \tag{5}
  $$

- *情况 3（卸载数据 SSTable）：* 如果仍未达到 $\alpha$，即 $C_{pm}=\frac{n-k}{k}\cdot C_{last}$，则 ELECT 进入情况 3。它选择尽可能大的 $C_{dm}$。需要注意的是，$C_{dm}\leq C_{last}$。根据公式 (3)，$C_{dm}$ 为：

  $$
  C_{dm}=\min\left\{C_{all}\cdot R\cdot\alpha-(R-1)\cdot C_{last},C_{last}\right\}. \tag{6}
  $$

sections.title: 5 Implementation
sections.originalMarkdown:
We implement ELECT in Java based on Cassandra v4.1.0 [3], with around 27 K lines of code of modifications to Cassandra’s codebase (which consists of 1.25 M lines of code), by adding redundancy transitioning, hotness monitoring, data offloading, full-node recovery, and degraded reads/writes.

We implement the erasure coding operations based on Intel’s Intelligent Storage Acceleration Library [27] and link the operations with Cassandra through the Java Native Interface.

**Consistent reads/writes.** Under replication, Cassandra supports consistent reads/writes based on the configurable read/write consistency levels, which specify the number of nodes in a replication group that need to acknowledge a read/write request. ELECT maintains the same read/write workflows for replicated KV pairs as in Cassandra. For writes, ELECT performs the same consistent writes as in Cassandra since it always writes KV pairs via replication. For reads, after receiving enough acknowledgments according to the read consistency level, if a KV pair is replicated, ELECT follows the same consistent read path as in Cassandra; if a KV pair is erasure-coded, ELECT always returns the KV pair from the primary LSM-tree or issues degraded reads (see below) if the KV pair is unavailable. ELECT currently does not verify reads for erasure-coded KV pairs.

**Full-node recovery.** Suppose that a node crashes and all its LSM-trees are lost. ELECT performs recovery in a new node on a per-LSM-tree basis. To recover a primary LSM-tree, ELECT retrieves the secondary LSM-tree from another alive node to the new node. The SSTables from the lowest to the second last level in the LSM-tree are replicated and can be directly recovered from their replicas. For the SSTables in the last level being erasure-coded, ELECT retrieves $k$ data or parity SSTables of the same coding group based on the ECMeta from the other alive nodes or the cloud to decode the lost SSTables. To recover a secondary LSM-tree, ELECT retrieves a primary LSM-tree or a secondary LSM-tree from the other nodes in the same replication group; if a primary LSM-tree is retrieved, ELECT removes the data components of SSTables that are erasure-coded, as the secondary LSM-tree only keeps their metadata components (§4.1.4).

**Degraded reads.** Suppose that ELECT receives a degraded read to an unavailable KV pair. ELECT relays the read request to another alive node in the same replication group, with a flag indicating the KV pair is unavailable. If the KV pair is stored with replication, the alive node directly returns the KV pair; otherwise, if the KV pair is stored with erasure coding, the alive node decodes the SSTable containing the KV pair by retrieving $k$ data or parity SSTables of the same coding group from the other alive nodes according to the ECMeta.

**Degraded writes.** Suppose that ELECT receives a degraded write to a failed node. It follows Cassandra to apply the *hinted handoff* mechanism [4], which allows the replay of a write to a failed node that returns online.

**Limitations.** ELECT does not support incremental recovery for individual SSTables as in Cassandra. Under replication, Cassandra builds a Merkle tree [41] in each node to detect inconsistencies among replicas for any failed SSTable recovery. Since ELECT includes erasure-coded SSTables in LSM-trees, it needs a revised Merkle tree that addresses both replication and erasure coding.

ELECT also does not currently support dynamic topology changes. We consider a possible approach for supporting topology changes in ELECT as follows. For replicated KV pairs, ELECT can relocate replicas when the nodes join or leave as in Cassandra. For erasure-coded KV pairs, ELECT can relocate some of the erasure-coded SSTables to keep them in consecutive nodes in the hash ring (§4.1.2). As in consistent hashing, ELECT should only relocate the KV pairs stored in the adjacent nodes of each joining/leaving node in the hash ring instead of all SSTables of the whole storage system, so as to mitigate the relocation overhead.
sections.translationMarkdown:
我们基于 Cassandra v4.1.0 [3] 使用 Java 实现了 ELECT，对 Cassandra 的代码库（包含 125 万行代码）修改了约 2.7 万行代码，加入了冗余转换、热度监控、数据卸载、整节点恢复以及降级读写。

我们基于 Intel Intelligent Storage Acceleration Library [27] 实现纠删码操作，并通过 Java Native Interface 将这些操作与 Cassandra 连接起来。

**一致性读写。** 在副本存储下，Cassandra 基于可配置的读写一致性级别来支持一致性读写；这些级别规定了复制组中需要确认读写请求的节点数量。对于采用副本存储的 KV pair，ELECT 保持与 Cassandra 相同的读写流程。对于写入，由于 ELECT 总是通过副本方式写入 KV pair，因此它执行与 Cassandra 相同的一致性写入。对于读取，在根据读取一致性级别收到足够数量的确认之后，如果 KV pair 采用副本存储，ELECT 会遵循与 Cassandra 相同的一致性读取路径；如果 KV pair 采用纠删码，ELECT 总是从主 LSM-tree 返回该 KV pair，或者在该 KV pair 不可用时发起降级读取（见下文）。ELECT 目前不对采用纠删码的 KV pair 执行读取验证。

**整节点恢复。** 假设一个节点崩溃，且其所有 LSM-tree 均丢失。ELECT 在新节点中以逐个 LSM-tree 的方式执行恢复。为了恢复一个主 LSM-tree，ELECT 将另一个存活节点上的次 LSM-tree 取回到新节点。LSM-tree 中从最低层到倒数第二层的 SSTable 采用副本存储，因此可以直接从其副本恢复。对于最后一层中采用纠删码的 SSTable，ELECT 根据 ECMeta，从其他存活节点或云端取回同一编码组中的 $k$ 个数据或奇偶校验 SSTable，以解码丢失的 SSTable。为了恢复一个次 LSM-tree，ELECT 从同一复制组的其他节点取回一个主 LSM-tree 或次 LSM-tree；如果取回的是主 LSM-tree，ELECT 会移除采用纠删码的 SSTable 的数据组件，因为次 LSM-tree 只保留它们的元数据组件（§4.1.4）。

**降级读取。** 假设 ELECT 收到针对某个不可用 KV pair 的降级读取请求。ELECT 将该读取请求转发给同一复制组中的另一个存活节点，并附带一个表明该 KV pair 不可用的标志。如果该 KV pair 采用副本存储，存活节点会直接返回该 KV pair；否则，如果该 KV pair 采用纠删码，存活节点会根据 ECMeta，从其他存活节点取回同一编码组中的 $k$ 个数据或奇偶校验 SSTable，并解码包含该 KV pair 的 SSTable。

**降级写入。** 假设 ELECT 收到针对故障节点的降级写入请求。它遵循 Cassandra 的做法，采用 *hinted handoff* 机制 [4]；当故障节点重新上线时，该机制允许向该节点重放写入。

**局限性。** ELECT 不像 Cassandra 那样支持针对单个 SSTable 的增量恢复。在副本存储下，Cassandra 在每个节点中构建 Merkle tree [41]，以检测副本之间的不一致，从而恢复任何发生故障的 SSTable。由于 ELECT 在 LSM-tree 中包含采用纠删码的 SSTable，因此它需要一种经过修改、能够同时处理副本和纠删码的 Merkle tree。

ELECT 目前也不支持动态拓扑变化。我们考虑了一种在 ELECT 中支持拓扑变化的可行方法，具体如下。对于采用副本存储的 KV pair，ELECT 可以像 Cassandra 一样，在节点加入或离开时重新定位副本。对于采用纠删码的 KV pair，ELECT 可以重新定位其中一部分采用纠删码的 SSTable，使它们继续位于哈希环中的连续节点上（§4.1.2）。与一致性哈希类似，ELECT 应当只重新定位哈希环中每个加入或离开节点的相邻节点所存储的 KV pair，而不是重新定位整个存储系统的所有 SSTable，从而减轻重新定位开销。

sections.title: 6 Evaluation
sections.originalMarkdown: We show via evaluation that ELECT reduces the storage overhead of Cassandra and maintains high performance.
sections.translationMarkdown: 我们通过评估表明，ELECT 降低了 Cassandra 的存储开销，同时保持了高性能。

sections.title: 6.1 Methodology
sections.originalMarkdown:
**Testbed.** We consider an edge-cloud setting, where the edge serves as the hot tier and the cloud serves as the cold tier. Specifically, we conduct evaluation on Alibaba Cloud [38]. We set up $M = 10$ edge nodes and multiple (up to 32) client nodes in the same geographical region. Each node is deployed on an ecs.i3g.2xlarge instance with eight 2.5 GHz vCPUs, 32 GiB RAM, 447 GiB SSD, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. All nodes are connected with a 3 Gbps network, with a network latency of no more than 1 ms. We also deploy the cloud on the Alibaba Object Storage Service in a different geographical region. Our measurement shows that the network latency between the two regions is at least 45 ms.

**Default settings.** We compare ELECT with the vanilla Cassandra. We configure Cassandra with triple replication ($R = 3$) and store all replicas in the edge nodes. We also configure ELECT with triple replication and the $(n, k) = (6, 4)$ RS code, and enable all features under a storage saving target $\alpha = 0.6$. For both systems, we fix the SSTable size as 4 MiB [28,64]. We disable SSTable compression for accurate storage size calculation. We set the read and write consistency levels as one and three, respectively (i.e., each of the reads and writes needs to be acknowledged by one node and all three replica nodes, respectively) for strong consistency. All other parameters remain the same as the defaults in Cassandra.

We use the benchmarking tool YCSB [16] to generate different types of workloads. By default, in Exp#1, we load 100 M 1-KiB KV pairs with 24-byte keys and 1000-byte values into storage before each experiment and generate 10 M requests; in the subsequent experiments that focus on examining the performance of individual KV operations, we load 10 M 1-KiB KV pairs and generate 1 M requests, while the performance trends remain stable as in Exp#1 even we use smaller workloads. In all experiments, the requests by default follow a Zipf distribution with a Zipfian constant of 0.99 (default in YCSB). Also, we run YCSB clients in two client nodes, each of which has eight YCSB client threads to simulate concurrent requests from multiple clients.

Our experiments consider normal (without failures) and degraded (with failures) modes. For degraded mode, we crash two edge nodes via the `kill -9` command.

We plot the average results over five runs, with error bars showing the 95% confidence intervals under the Student’s t-distribution (note that some error bars may be invisible due to small deviations).
sections.translationMarkdown:
**测试平台。** 我们考虑一种 edge-cloud 环境，其中 edge 作为 hot tier，cloud 作为 cold tier。具体而言，我们在 Alibaba Cloud [38] 上进行评估。我们在同一地理区域内搭建 $M = 10$ 个 edge 节点和多个（最多 32 个）client 节点。每个节点均部署在 ecs.i3g.2xlarge 实例上，配备 8 个 2.5 GHz vCPU、32 GiB RAM、447 GiB SSD，并运行 Ubuntu 22.04 LTS。所有节点均通过 3 Gbps 网络连接，网络延迟不超过 1 ms。我们还将 cloud 部署在另一地理区域的 Alibaba Object Storage Service 上。测量结果表明，两个区域之间的网络延迟至少为 45 ms。

**默认设置。** 我们将 ELECT 与原版 Cassandra 进行比较。我们为 Cassandra 配置三副本（$R = 3$），并将所有副本存储在 edge 节点。我们还为 ELECT 配置三副本和 $(n, k) = (6, 4)$ RS code，并在存储节省目标 $\alpha = 0.6$ 下启用全部功能。对于两个系统，我们都将 SSTable 大小固定为 4 MiB [28,64]。为准确计算存储大小，我们禁用 SSTable 压缩。为实现强一致性，我们将读、写一致性级别分别设置为 1 和 3（即每次读需要一个节点确认，而每次写需要全部三个副本节点确认）。其余所有参数均保持 Cassandra 的默认值。

我们使用基准测试工具 YCSB [16] 生成不同类型的工作负载。默认情况下，在 Exp#1 中，我们在每次实验前向存储系统加载 100 M 个 1-KiB KV pair（key 为 24 byte，value 为 1000 byte），并生成 10 M 个请求；在后续专门考察单项 KV 操作性能的实验中，我们加载 10 M 个 1-KiB KV pair 并生成 1 M 个请求。即使使用较小的工作负载，性能趋势仍与 Exp#1 一致。在所有实验中，请求默认服从 Zipf 分布，Zipfian constant 为 0.99（YCSB 默认值）。此外，我们在两个 client 节点上运行 YCSB client，每个节点运行 8 个 YCSB client thread，以模拟来自多个 client 的并发请求。

我们的实验考虑 normal mode（无故障）和 degraded mode（有故障）。在 degraded mode 下，我们通过 `kill -9` 命令使两个 edge 节点崩溃。

我们绘制五次运行结果的平均值，误差棒表示 Student’s t-distribution 下的 95% 置信区间（请注意，由于偏差很小，某些误差棒可能不可见）。

sections.originalMarkdown:
**Exp#1 (YCSB core workloads).** We first compare the overall storage overhead and performance of Cassandra and ELECT using the six YCSB core workloads [16], namely A (50% reads, 50% writes), B (95% reads, 5% writes), C (100% reads), D (95% reads, 5% writes), E (95% scans, 5% writes), and F (50% reads, 50% read-modify-writes). Each workload (except D) follows a Zipf distribution, while Workload D reads the latest written KV pairs. For ELECT, we measure both edge-only and overall edge-cloud storage sizes.

*Figure 5: Exp#1: YCSB core workloads. Throughput results are normalized by Cassandra’s throughput (above each bar) in KOPS.*

Figure 5 shows the storage size and throughput results. ELECT achieves 56.1% storage savings (in the edge only) and 39.1% overall storage savings (in both the edge and cloud) compared with Cassandra. The actual edge storage savings of ELECT are slightly less than $\alpha = 0.6$, as it also maintains metadata components for deleted KV pairs in the secondary LSM-trees after redundancy transitioning. The metadata components of LSM-trees in ELECT account for 6.9% of its edge storage size (not shown in the figure); note that no metadata components are offloaded to the cloud (§4.2).

In terms of performance, both Cassandra and ELECT have similar throughput (with up to 3% differences) in all workloads except E. For Workload E, which is scan-intensive, ELECT achieves a 2.84× throughput gain over Cassandra. The reason is that ELECT reduces individual LSM-tree sizes and hence I/O amplification through decoupled replication management, so the number of SSTables being accessed is also reduced [57,68]. Such reduced access overhead has more prominent performance improvements to scans, which read a range of KV pairs.

**Exp#2 (Benchmarking of KV operations).** We evaluate the average latencies of specific KV operations, including reads, writes, scans, and updates. We load 10 M 1-KiB KV pairs and issue 1 M requests for each type of KV operations (§6.1). We consider both normal and degraded modes. For degraded mode, we measure the performance of all requests (including normal and degraded requests) when the system is in degraded mode with edge node failures. For example, if a read encounters a non-failed node, it is a normal read; if it encounters a failed node, it becomes a degraded read and ELECT recovers the SSTable that contains the requested key.

*Figure 6: Exp#2: Benchmarking of KV operations. Results are normalized by Cassandra’s latencies (above each bar) in milliseconds.*

Figure 6 shows the results. Note that Cassandra keeps almost identical performance in both normal and degraded modes as it keeps all replicated storage in the edge. In normal mode (Figure 6(a)), ELECT maintains similar performance as in Cassandra in reads, writes, and updates with up to 2.7% of higher average latencies; it reduces the average scan latency of Cassandra by 21.5% (see Exp#1). In degraded mode (Figure 6(b)), ELECT still has similar performance of Cassandra in writes and updates with up to 3.3% higher average latencies and reduces the average scan latency of Cassandra by 21.1%. However, ELECT incurs a latency increase of 5.32× in reads over Cassandra, mainly due to the retrieval of SSTables from the cloud to the edge for recovery if the degraded reads are issued to the KV pairs in the last LSM-tree level.

We further examine the read and scan results in degraded mode. For reads, we observe that both Cassandra and ELECT have very similar 99th-percentile latencies at about 1.7 ms (not shown in the figure), meaning that most reads can be served in the edge and have small latency differences. Some degraded reads need to retrieve SSTables from the cloud, and such requests increase the average read latency in degraded mode. Unlike reads, ELECT still shows performance gains in scans (which include normal and degraded reads to a range of KV pairs) as in normal mode. The reason is that most unavailable SSTables are recovered in the early stage of scans, so the overall adverse impact on scans is much mitigated as opposed to reads.

sections.title: 6.3 System-level Analysis
sections.originalMarkdown:
**Exp#3 (Performance breakdown).** We break down the performance of writes, reads in normal mode, and reads in degraded mode. Each write comprises (i) writing to the WAL, (ii) writing to the MemTable, (iii) flushing the MemTable, (iv) compaction, (v) redundancy transitioning, and (vi) data offloading. Each read in normal or degraded mode comprises (i) reading from the MemTable, (ii) reading from the block cache, (iii) reading from SSTables, and (iv) recovery (for degraded reads). We measure the time of each step across all nodes and obtain the average results on processing 1 MiB of writes/reads based on the workloads as described in §6.1. Since the steps are performed in parallel, the actual time spent on an operation is less than the sum of times of all steps.

*Table 1: Exp#3: Performance breakdown. We show the average latency of each step for processing 1 MiB of writes/reads and the corresponding 95% confidence interval.*

| Operation | Step | Cassandra | ELECT |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Write | WAL | 21.32 ± 0.76 ms | 21.84 ± 0.28 ms |
| Write | MemTable | 37.98 ± 1.73 ms | 40.84 ± 0.13 ms |
| Write | Flushing | 16.95 ± 0.29 ms | 17.70 ± 0.18 ms |
| Write | Compaction | 205.87 ± 2.21 ms | 169.03 ± 3.23 ms |
| Write | Transitioning | - | 239.05 ± 2.69 ms |
| Write | Offloading | - | 162.84 ± 12.05 ms |
| Read in normal mode | Cache | 17.05 ± 0.27 ms | 17.41 ± 0.33 ms |
| Read in normal mode | MemTable | 18.35 ± 0.34 ms | 18.75 ± 0.18 ms |
| Read in normal mode | SSTables | 20.78 ± 0.95 ms | 21.54 ± 0.66 ms |
| Read in degraded mode | Cache | 23.20 ± 0.61 ms | 23.38 ± 0.46 ms |
| Read in degraded mode | MemTable | 182.69 ± 2.53 ms | 184.39 ± 1.67 ms |
| Read in degraded mode | SSTables | 177.55 ± 0.60 ms | 184.14 ± 2.35 ms |
| Read in degraded mode | Recovery | - | 1957.64 ± 34.16 ms |

Table 1 shows the performance breakdown. Most common steps in Cassandra and ELECT have similar latencies, except for compaction in writes, ELECT has a smaller latency by 17.9%. The reason is that ELECT decouples replication management into multiple LSM-trees and reduces the I/O amplifications in compaction [57, 68]. The redundancy transitioning has the highest average latency among all steps, while the offloading has a low average latency since only a fraction of data is transmitted from the edge to the cloud. However, both redundancy transitioning and data offloading are performed in the background and incur limited overhead to writes, so ELECT has similar write performance as Cassandra (see Exp#1 and Exp#2).

For reads in normal mode, both Cassandra and ELECT have similar performance in each step. For reads in degraded mode, ELECT is bottlenecked by the recovery step (with 1957.64 ms per MiB).

**Exp#4 (Full-node recovery).** We evaluate full-node recovery in Cassandra and ELECT. We crash one edge node, delete all its data, start a new edge node, and use the `nodetool` command to recover all lost data into the new edge node. We evaluate the recovery performance of different loaded data sizes, including 10 GiB, 20 GiB, and 30 GiB (i.e., 10 M, 20 M, and 30 M 1-KiB KV pairs). For fair comparisons, we disable the Merkle tree operation in Cassandra (which is not supported in ELECT (§5)). Figure 7 shows the full-node recovery times. The recovery times of Cassandra and ELECT increase almost linearly. ELECT incurs about 50% higher recovery time than Cassandra since it needs to retrieve data and parity SSTables from other edge nodes or the cloud to decode the lost SSTables in the primary LSM-tree.

*Figure 7: Exp#4: Full-node recovery time.*

We further provide a breakdown of the full-node recovery time of ELECT into three steps: (i) copying replicated SSTables from other edge nodes; (ii) retrieving data and parity SSTables for decoding; and (iii) decoding the lost SSTables. Table 2 shows the full-node recovery time breakdown of ELECT for 30 GiB data. The recovery performance is network-bound, in which retrieving the data and parity SSTables occupies 93.3% of the total recovery time.

*Table 2: Exp#4: Recovery time breakdown for 30 GiB data.*

| Steps | Time |
|---|---:|
| Copy | 13.54 ± 0.22 s |
| Retrieve | 373.98 ± 11.61 s |
| Decode | 13.34 ± 0.48 s |

**Exp#5 (Resource usage).** We compare the CPU usage, memory usage, disk I/O size, and network traffic of Cassandra and ELECT. We consider three settings: (i) loading KV pairs until the SSTables reach a stable state, (ii) running in normal mode without failures, and (iii) running in degraded mode with two node failures. After loading KV pairs, we issue 1 M requests, including reads, writes, updates, and scans, with one-fourth of all requests each. We measure the CPU usage, memory usage, disk I/O, and network usage in all alive edge nodes through the Linux system tools, namely `top`, `free`, `iostat`, and `iftop`, respectively. We collect the resource usage data every 1 s. We show the 95th-percentile CPU usage and memory usage as well as the overall disk I/O size and network traffic size.

*Figure 8: Exp#5: Resource usage. All results are normalized by Cassandra’s actual resource usage results (numbered atop the bars), including CPU usage (%), memory usage (GiB), disk I/O size (GiB), and network traffic (GiB).*

Figure 8 shows the results. Figure 8(a) shows that ELECT has 23.4% and 23.3% less 95th-percentile CPU usage than Cassandra in load and degraded operations, respectively. ELECT mainly performs network transmissions in redundancy transitioning and data offloading, both of which involve less CPU usage (in each 1-second interval). However, ELECT has long durations in both redundancy transitioning and data offloading (Table 1), so its total CPU time is still higher than Cassandra’s. Figure 8(b) shows that ELECT slightly increases the 95th-percentile memory usage by 7.0% during the load operation, since it needs extra memory space for erasure coding. It also slightly reduces the memory usage in normal and degraded modes by 4.9% and 5.1%, respectively, as it reduces the LSM-tree size through decoupled replication management. Figure 8(c) shows that ELECT reduces the disk I/O size of Cassandra by 23.6% in the load operation, as it reduces the LSM-tree size and hence I/O amplifications through decoupled replication management, and also reduces the compaction overhead of the secondary LSM-trees by writing fewer KV pairs to the last LSM-tree level. Note that ELECT still has higher disk I/O size in degraded mode than in normal mode due to the reconstruction overhead in erasure coding. Figure 8(d) shows that ELECT has similar network traffic to Cassandra in normal mode, while it incurs 22.1% and 6.3% higher network traffic than Cassandra in load and degraded operations, respectively. In the load operation, ELECT distributes SSTables for redundancy transitioning and offloads SSTables to the cloud; in degraded mode, it retrieves SSTables to recover unavailable SSTables.

| 步骤 | 时间 |
|---|---:|
| Copy | 13.54 ± 0.22 s |
| Retrieve | 373.98 ± 11.61 s |
| Decode | 13.34 ± 0.48 s |

**Exp#5（资源使用量）。** 我们比较 Cassandra 和 ELECT 的 CPU 使用率、内存使用量、磁盘 I/O 大小和网络流量。我们考虑三种设置：(i) 加载 KV pair，直至 SSTable 达到稳定状态；(ii) 在无故障的 normal mode 下运行；以及 (iii) 在两个节点故障的 degraded mode 下运行。加载 KV pair 后，我们发出 1 M 个请求，其中 read、write、update 和 scan 各占四分之一。我们分别使用 Linux 系统工具 `top`、`free`、`iostat` 和 `iftop` 测量所有存活 edge 节点的 CPU 使用率、内存使用量、磁盘 I/O 和网络使用量。我们每 1 s 收集一次资源使用数据。我们展示 CPU 使用率和内存使用量的 95th percentile，以及磁盘 I/O 总量和网络流量总量。

*图 8：Exp#5：资源使用量。所有结果均按 Cassandra 的实际资源使用结果归一化（数值标注于柱上方），包括 CPU 使用率（%）、内存使用量（GiB）、磁盘 I/O 大小（GiB）和网络流量（GiB）。*
